components: renal; hepatic or icterus; cerebral; pulmonary; pancreatitis; rhabdomyolysis
definition: Classified at admission on clinical and laboratory data. Complicated if any of: renal dysfunction (creatinine >155 umol/L without pre-renal azotaemia), hepatic involvement (ALT >176 U/L and AP >360 U/L), CNS dysfunction (modified Glasgow coma scale <9), respiratory dysfunction (radiographic pulmonary oedema or increased respiratory effort), pancreatic dysfunction (SNAP cPL), muscular involvement (CPK >600 U/L). Complications seen: muscular 7/11, respiratory 4/11, pancreatic 1/11, hepatic 1/11. Dogs with co-infection excluded.
quote: the affected dogs were divided into two groups, complicated (N = 11) and uncomplicated (N = 19) babesiosis.

components: MODS; renal; pulmonary; hepatic or icterus; rhabdomyolysis; cerebral
definition_source: author-defined (Table 1 criteria; modified Glasgow coma scale from Welzl et al.)
definition: Dogs with MODS (two or more organ dysfunctions by the Table 1 criteria: creatinine >180 umol/L, dyspnoea/pulmonary oedema, ALT/AP/bilirubin thresholds, CPK >600 U/L, modified Glasgow coma scale <9) vs dogs with none of the listed complications. Pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests.
quote: In dogs with complicated babesiosis, 6 (54.55%) had single organ dysfunction and 5 (45.45%) dogs had MODS.

components: MODS; renal; pulmonary; hepatic or icterus; rhabdomyolysis; cerebral
definition: Dogs with MODS vs dogs with a single organ dysfunction (Table 1 criteria). Pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests.
quote: In dogs with complicated babesiosis, 6 (54.55%) had single organ dysfunction and 5 (45.45%) dogs had MODS.

components: renal; pulmonary; hepatic or icterus; rhabdomyolysis; cerebral
definition: Dogs with exactly one organ dysfunction by the Table 1 criteria vs dogs with none. Pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests.
quote: Uncomplicated babesiosis was diagnosed in 29 (72.5%) and complicated babesiosis in the remaining 11 dogs (27.5%).

definition: Dogs that died despite treatment (all had MODS) vs survivors; related to admission biomarkers by Kendall Tau-b correlation. Whether any death was euthanasia and the follow-up horizon are not stated.
quote: Treatment was successful in all dogs without development of any complications as well as in 7 cases of complicated babesiosis, while 4 dogs with MODS died despite treatment (mortality rate 10%).

definition: Anaemia by haematocrit: non-anaemic HCT >37% vs anaemic (HCT <=37%: mild 30-37%, moderate 18-29%, severe <18%).
quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

definition: Moderately anaemic (HCT 18-29%) vs mildly anaemic (HCT 30-37%). The one severely anaemic dog was not analysed.
quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

definition: Degree of anaemia as continuous HCT (%) in the 40 infected dogs; Spearman rank correlation with each biomarker. Lower HCT = more severe anaemia.
quote: Also, there was a significant positive correlation of HCT with GPx and SOD, whereas significant negative correlation of HCT with MDA (Table 6).

components: SIRS; MODS; renal; hepatic or icterus; pulmonary; rhabdomyolysis
definition_source: WHO malaria classification; SIRS and MODS criteria
definition: Complicated babesiosis classified on clinical and laboratory data following the WHO malaria classification; main complications SIRS (>=2 of 4 criteria) and MODS (>=2 of renal creatinine >180 umol/l, hepatic ALT >176 and AP >360 IU/l, respiratory pulmonary oedema or dyspnoea, muscular CPK >600 IU/l). 66% of complicated dogs had MODS, all of them SIRS positive. 1 complicated dog died before day 7.
quote: On the basis of clinical manifestations and laboratory data the infected dogs were classified into two subgroups: complicated (18 dogs, 8 Female, 10 Male) and uncomplicated (13 dogs, 5 Female, 8 Male).

components: score; renal; hepatic or icterus; hypoglycaemia; other
definition_source: author-defined (criteria drawn from Bohm et al., Keller et al., Nel et al., Schoeman et al.)
definition: Author-built cumulative score, 1 point each for: basal cortisol > 275 nmol/L, ACTH > 20 pg/mL, T4 < 2.8 nmol/L, albumin < 20, potassium < 3.6 mmol/L, phosphate > 1.94 mmol/L, creatinine > 133 umol/L, bile acids >= 55 umol/L, glucose < 3.3 mmol/L, icterus, band cells > 10%, body temperature < 37.8 C (maximum 12). 'other' covers the endocrine, electrolyte, albumin, band-cell and hypothermia items. Observed range 0-10, median 2 (n = 34).
quote: The severity of the babesiosis cases was scored using the following parameters, with each criteria receiving a score of 1:

components: cerebral; hepatic or icterus; renal; coagulopathy; hypotension or shock; MODS; death
definition: Three groups of 17 nested-PCR-positive dogs classified by clinical severity: subclinical carriers, mild uncomplicated babesiosis, complicated babesiosis (epilepsy/cerebral, jaundice, renal failure, septic shock with DIC and death, MODS and death). 5 of the 17 complicated dogs died.
quote: dogs manifesting mild symptoms of simple or uncomplicated babesiosis (group-2) and lastly, dogs manifesting symptoms of complicated babesiosis (group-3)

definition: Short-term outcome: survival to discharge vs death or euthanasia due to poor prognosis. 34/320 died; all treated dogs that died did so within 24 h of admission.
quote: Outcome was recorded as short-term survival (i.e. until discharge), or death/euthanasia due to poor prognosis.

definition: Collapse at presentation = unable to stand unaided (72/320). Used by the authors as a severity grouping for many laboratory comparisons.
quote: Seventy-two of the 320 cases (22.5%) were collapsed at presentation (unable to stand unaided).

severity_label: Spec cPL concentration (>400 µg/l = suspected pancreatitis)
definition_source: IDEXX Spec cPL reference cut-off (>400 µg/l)
severe_group: dogs with cPL >400 µg/l (n=2); correlation over all dogs
definition: Serum Spec cPL concentration analysed as a continuous measure of pancreatic injury; concentrations >400 µg/l were taken to indicate pancreatitis (2 of 20 dogs). Correlations across all 20 dogs.
quote: The reference interval was set at <200 µg/l and concentrations >400 µg/l were considered to indicate pancreatitis.

definition: Serum lipase activity (reference 13-200 U/l) analysed as a continuous pancreatic measure; all 20 dogs exceeded 200 U/l.
quote: As shown in Fig. 2, all dogs had lipase activity greater than 200 U/l.

definition: Short-term outcome: survival to discharge vs death or euthanasia due to poor prognosis during hospitalisation. 15/140 died.
quote: Outcome was noted as short-term survival (i.e., until discharge from hospital), or death/euthanasia due to poor prognosis during hospitalization.

severity_label: fatal babesiosis (confirmed or suspected) vs subclinical infection or mild disease
comparison_group: mild disease (n=3) or subclinical / non-specific signs (n=12)
definition: Among 18 community dogs positive for Babesia spp. on blood smear (13 confirmed B. rossi by PCR-RLB), fatal babesiosis was confirmed in one juvenile and suspected in one juvenile and one probably very old adult; the other dogs had transient mild disease (3 adults) or no or non-specific clinical signs (9 adults, 3 juveniles). Case-series description; no statistical comparison.
quote: Fatal babesiosis was confirmed in one juvenile (dog 10) and suspected in one other juvenile (dog 15) and one (probably) very old

components: collapse; hypotension or shock; haemoconcentration; renal; hypoglycaemia; hepatic or icterus; cerebral; pulmonary; other
definition_source: Jacobson and Clark 1994; Jacobson 2006; WHO 2014 severe falciparum malaria criteria
definition: Complicated = at least one complication at presentation or during hospitalisation: collapse (unable to walk unaided), hypotension (MAP <80 mmHg), severe anaemia (Hct <0.15), haemoconcentration (Hct >0.37 with intravascular haemolysis), secondary IMHA (positive in-saline agglutination), AKI (IRIS grading), hypoglycaemia (<3.3 mmol/L), jaundice (bilirubin >50 umol/L), cerebral babesiosis, ARDS. 'other' = severe anaemia and secondary IMHA.
quote: Dogs were diagnosed with complicated babesiosis when at least one of the following complications were diagnosed either at presentation or during hospitalization.

severity_label: complicated (C) vs uncomplicated (UC) B. canis infection
definition: Dogs with B. canis infection admitted to the University clinic in Kosice were divided on clinical and laboratory findings into uncomplicated (lethargy, anorexia, pale mucous membranes, icterus, haemoglobinuria, splenomegaly) and complicated forms; complicated cases were associated with SIRS and MODS, and seven dogs of the complicated group died. Exact criteria for each complication not given.
quote: the dogs were divided into a group with uncomplicated (group UC, 25 dogs) and complicated (group C, 15 dogs) form of B. canis infection

severity_label: group C (azotaemic, UPC > 1) vs group B (non-azotaemic, UPC > 0.5) vs group A (non-azotaemic, UPC < 0.5)
definition_source: author-defined (creatinine 140 umol/L and ACVIM proteinuria UPC thresholds)
comparison_group: group A, non-azotaemic with UPC < 0.5 (n=6); group B (n=10) intermediate
definition: Three ordered groups of B. canis dogs by kidney function at admission: A, serum creatinine < 140 umol/L and UPC < 0.5 (n=6); B, non-azotaemic with UPC > 0.5 (n=10); C, azotaemic (creatinine > 140 umol/L) with UPC > 1 (n=6). Severe = group C; comparison = group A unless stated. UPC thresholds follow ACVIM/IRIS guidance cited in the introduction.
quote: group A consisted of six non-azotemic dogs (serum creatinine < 140 μmol/L) with a normal urine protein to creatinine ratio (UPC < 0.5); group B of 10 non-azotemic dogs with UPC > 0.5; and group C of six azotemic dogs (serum creatinine > 140 μmol/L) with UPC > 1.

complication: renal proteinuria (UPC as a continuous measure)
definition: Pearson correlation of targeted urinary metabolites with UPC, used by the authors as the conventional measure of kidney dysfunction. Whether healthy controls were included in the correlation is not stated.
quote: Correlations between the metabolites identified by the targeted approach and UPC (conventional parameter) were calculated by Pearson’s correlation coefficient.

definition: ROC analysis of targeted urinary metabolites 'in detecting kidney dysfunction'. The positive and negative groups of the ROC are not stated (probably groups B and C vs group A and/or controls).
quote: receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were applied to investigate the clinical diagnostic potentials of these metabolites.

definition: Dog status recorded as died or live in Table 1 (police dog survey). Among the 62 Babesia-infected dogs, 53 died and 9 were alive. Cause of death, follow-up period and euthanasia not stated.

Venous parasitaemia (%) over the course of experimental infection, used by the authors as an indicator of disease severity; markers correlated with it by Spearman rank correlation across serial samples. Severity component is parasite burden (other).
quote: we aimed to investigate changes in markers of inflammation (cytokine concentrations, neutrophil count, monocyte count and CRP) and indicators of disease severity (including habitus, appetite, vital parameters, parasitaemia and hematocrit) over time

severity_label: dog that died vs surviving dogs
definition: One high dose dog died unexpectedly at about 96 hours, around the time of treatment; the other four inoculated dogs recovered.
quote: Due to the unexpected death of one dog in the HD group, to avoid any further losses, the LD group was treated 12 hours later (at 108 hours)

severity_label: high dose (HD) vs low dose (LD) group
definition: Experimental infection dose groups; all HD dogs (10^8 parasitised RBC) developed collapse (inability to stand unaided, habitus score 1+) and were treated at 96 h; no LD dog (10^4) collapsed or reached a predetermined end point. Severity contrast by dose that coincides with collapse ('other' = inoculum dose).
quote: collapsed (defined as the inability to stand unaided), whilst none of the dogs in the LD group were ever collapsed, nor reached any of the predetermined end points.

definition: Dogs that died (3) or were euthanised (4; including financial reasons with acute renal failure) vs 39 survivors among the 46 clinic dogs.
quote: Thirty‐nine dogs (85%) survived. Four dogs were euthanized after 2 to 18 days

components: anaemia grade; hepatic or icterus; renal
definition: Severity classification based on Bajer et al. (2016): anaemia (RBC), hepatic (AST/ALT/ALP) and renal (urea) scores 0-2; any score 2 = severe (level 3, n=44 of 82); more than one dysfunction at level 1 = moderate (n=16); one group of signs = mild (n=22). For gene expression, a random subset of 32 B. canis dogs was split into Babesia 1 (mild and moderate) and Babesia 2 (severe); subset group sizes not stated.
quote: B. canis-infected dogs with mild and moderate babesiosis (representing classes 0 and 1) were combined into the group referred to as ‘Babesia 1’ and dogs with severe babesiosis (class 2) were assigned to ‘Babesia 2’.

severity_label: anaemia level 2 (RBC <4.5 T/l) vs level 0 (RBC 5.5-8.0 T/l)
severe_group: B. canis dogs at anaemia level 2 (n not stated)
comparison_group: B. canis dogs at anaemia level 0 (n not stated)
definition: Anaemia severity score from RBC count: 0 = 5.5-8.0 T/l, 1 = 4.5-5.5 T/l, 2 = below 4.5 T/l. Rows use the B. canis-only column of Table 3 (level 2 vs level 0).
quote: a. severity of anaemia (severity score 0—RBC counts within normal range 5.5–8.0 T/l; severity score 1—RBC counts in a range 4.5–5.5 T/l; severity score 2—RBC below 4.5 T/l)

severe_group: B. canis dogs at hepatic level 2 (n not stated)
comparison_group: B. canis dogs at hepatic level 0 (n not stated)
definition: Hepatic score from AST, ALT and ALP: within reference range = 0, above (up to 100 U/l) = 1, profoundly above (>100 U/l) = 2. Rows use the B. canis-only column of Table 3.
quote: b. hepatic dysfunction parameters (measures of enzymes activity) based on reference values for AST– aspartate aminotransferase, ALT- alanine aminotransferase and ALP- alkaline phosphatase within, above (up to 100 U/l) and profoundly above (> 100 U/l) the normal range, representing scores of 0, 1 and 2, respectively (Table 2)

severe_group: B. canis dogs at renal level 2 (n not stated)
comparison_group: B. canis dogs at renal level 0 (n not stated)
definition: Renal score from serum urea: within reference = 0, above (up to 100 mg/dl) = 1, profoundly above (>100 mg/dl) = 2. Rows use the B. canis-only column of Table 3.
quote: c. renal dysfunction parameters (based on reference values for serum urea) within, above (up to 100 mg/dl) and profoundly above (> 100 mg/dl) the normal range, representing severity scores of 0, 1 and 2, respectively (Table 2).

components: collapse; cerebral; death; anaemia grade; haemoconcentration; renal; hepatic or icterus; hypoglycaemia; hyperlactataemia; other
definition: Complicated if clinical collapse, cerebral signs (seizures, coma) or death within 24 h of admission, or any of: haematocrit <0.15 or >0.5 L/L, urea >13 mmol/L, creatinine >120 umol/L, total bilirubin >30 umol/L, glucose <3.3 mmol/L, lactate >5 mmol/L, band neutrophils >1.5 x 10^9/L. Uncomplicated dogs met none. PCR-RLB confirmed B. rossi mono-infection.
quote: Dogs were classified as having complicated babesiosis on the basis of clinical signs and clinical pathology. Clinical signs included: clinical signs of collapse, signs of cerebral disease (seizures, coma) or death within 24 h of admission.

components: death; collapse; renal; haemoconcentration; cerebral; pulmonary; other
definition_source: author-defined (complicated babesiosis per Jacobson and Clark 1994; Leisewitz et al. 2019)
definition: Retrospective OVAH cohort 2013-2021, dogs >= 6 months, first episodes. Severe if any of: death, hospitalisation of 2 or more days, blood transfusion, collapse (unable to walk unassisted), renal failure, haematocrit <= 15 or >= 55, seizures with glucose > 3.3 mmol/L, body temperature <= 36 C, ARDS. 'other' = hospitalisation >= 2 days, transfusion, haematocrit <= 15 (severe anaemia), hypothermia. Authors equate it with complicated babesiosis.
quote: The outcome was categorized as severe if any of the following conditions were met:

severity_label: severe vs moderate vs mild anaemia (vs normal HCT)
definition: Anaemia graded by haematocrit: severe HCT < 20%, moderate 20% <= HCT < 30%, mild 30% <= HCT < 37.3%. Severe n=46, moderate n=22, mild n=21, normal HCT n=19.
quote: Severity of anemia was classified based on HCT as severe (HCT < 20%), moderate (20% ≤ HCT < 30%), and mild (30% ≤ HCT < 37.3%).

definition: Author-defined hematological score: points for mild (+1), moderate (+2), marked (+3) anaemia, thrombocytopenia and leukopenia, +1 leukocytosis, +3 pancytopenia. Continuous score; higher = more severe clinicopathological alterations. Not a clinical outcome.
quote: A hematological score (HES) was calculated by summing the severities of each cytopenia (0 = not present, + 1 = mild, + 2 = moderate, + 3 = marked) as well as the presence of leukocytosis (> 12.0 G/l, 0 = not present, + 1 = present), and pancytopenia (0 = not present, + 3 = present).

definition: Short-term outcome: survival to discharge vs death or euthanasia due to poor prognosis (dogs euthanised for other reasons excluded). Median time to death 24 (24-48) h.
quote: Outcome was recorded as short-term survival (i.e., survival until discharge) or death/euthanasia due to poor prognosis.

definition: Death or euthanasia among the 193 dogs with outcome information (mortality 6.7%).
quote: Thirteen dogs died (mortality rate: 6.7%, 95% CI: 4.0–11.2%).

definition: Course reported by the treating veterinarian as complicated or uncomplicated; complications not defined.
quote: Uncomplicated courses were reported in 169 of 193 dogs (87.6%, 95% CI: 82.2–91.5%), complicated courses in 24 of 193 dogs (12.4%, 95% CI: 8.5–17.8%).

definition_source: author-defined (RBC reference range, Kraft and Dürr 2005)
definition: Dogs with babesiosis split by RBC count at admission: decreased (<5.5 T/l, n=23) vs within the physiological range (5.5-8.5 T/l, n=14).
quote: According to the RBC count, the dogs sufferring from babesiosis were categorized into 2 groups

definition: Dogs that died spontaneously during the disease; horizon not stated.
quote: Seven of the total number of dogs with babesiosis died spontaneously

severity_label: high vs medium vs low intensity of invasion
comparison_group: low intensity of invasion (n=35); medium n=38
definition: Intensity of invasion graded from capillary smears by affected erythrocytes per microscope field and parasites per erythrocyte: high (5,38±0,12 per field, 3-5 per RBC), medium (1,89±0,05, 1-3), low (1-5 per smear, 1-2). Rows compare high (severe) with low.
quote: We studied the features of the clinical manifestation of the disease depending on the intensity of invasion (II) (Table 1).

definition: Dogs followed during the treatment period and classified by survival. Euthanasia not mentioned.
quote: All the infected dogs were followed up during the treatment period for their survivability and they were classified into survivors (n=18) and non-survivors (n=14) of infection.

severe_group: jaundiced form (experimental group n=20; n per form not stated)
comparison_group: anaemic form (experimental group n=20; n per form not stated)
definition: Authors describe acute spontaneous babesiosis as successive forms: anaemic (early, without jaundice) and jaundiced (late, icterus from about day 3, worse condition, reported mortality about 40%). Blood was tested at both stages in the experimental group of 20 dogs; it is not stated whether the two columns are the same dogs at two times or different dogs.
quote: Blood tests of dogs with acute spontaneous babesiosis were performed at different stages of the disease, which were defined as anemic (early) and jaundiced (late) forms. It was found that the changes found in sick animals are dynamically deteriorating and in the jaundiced form is more severe than in the anemic.

severity_label: acute (complicated form) vs chronic (mild, non-specific) vs subclinical (apparently healthy)
comparison_group: chronic infection (n=8 with labs; 11 overall) and subclinical (n=3 with labs; 4 overall)
definition: 34 PCR-positive B. gibsoni dogs classed by clinical signs from the submitting clinic's records: Group I acute = signs of the complicated form (n=19), Group II chronic = mild to non-specific signs (n=11), Group III subclinical = apparently healthy (n=4). Labs available for 15/8/3. No explicit criteria list; complications named in Table 2 include IMHA and pancreatitis ('other').
quote: dogs manifesting symptoms of the complicated form of canine babesiosis (Group I – acute infection), dogs with mild to non-specific symptoms (Group II – chronic infection), and apparently healthy dogs (Group III – subclinical infection)

definition: Death vs survival among the 80 anaemic Babesia dogs; follow-up horizon and euthanasia not stated.
quote: Among the anemic dogs, the mortality rate was 18 (22.5%).

definition: Anaemia (PCV below 36%, graded mild 30-36%, moderate 20-29%, severe < 20%) vs no anaemia among 103 Babesia-positive dogs.
quote: Moreover, a total of 80 (77.7%) dogs exhibited anemia

definition: Groups formed by the intensity of erythrocyte parasitisation on Romanowsky-Giemsa smears per 100 erythrocytes: low intensity ('+', 1-2 affected erythrocytes) vs high intensity ('+++'); dogs with medium intensity ('++') were not included. The printed criterion for '+++' is internally inconsistent ('up to 1-4 erythrocytes'); the text adds that at high intensity 4-6 or more parasites were seen in one cell. All Labrador dogs.
quote: Experimental groups were formed from animals with only low and high-intensity of infection.

definition: Survival vs non-survival based on response to treatment; horizon and euthanasia not stated. Population restricted to dogs with SIRS, severe sepsis or septic shock.
quote: The dogs were split into two groups as survivors and non survivors based on the treatment response.

severity_label: anaemic vs non-anaemic dogs with babesiosis
definition: PCR-confirmed Babesia-infected dogs grouped as anaemic or non-anaemic on haemoglobin, PCV and erythrocyte count (cut-offs not stated), sampled on the first day of presentation.
quote: the affected animals were grouped into anaemic (n = 58, Male - 25, Female – 33) and non-anaemic group (n = 50, Male - 22, Female – 28)

severity_label: degree of anaemia (haemoglobin, PCV, erythrocyte count as continuous measures)
definition: Continuous haemoglobin, PCV and erythrocyte count across all 108 infected dogs, used as measures of anaemia severity in Pearson correlations with LHD.
quote: Pearson correlation between LHD and other standard anaemic parameters revealed the significant (P<0.01) negative relationship of LHD to haemoglobin, packed cell volume, erythrocytes, MCHC and serum iron (Fig. 2).

severity_label: stage I / stage II / stage III of acute babesiosis
definition: Author-defined stages of acute B. canis babesiosis by duration of disease and invasion intensity (parasitaemia): stage I 1-2 days and 2-4%; stage II 3-4 days and 5-8%; stage III 5-6 days and >9%. Components = 'other': disease duration and parasitaemia. Pairwise rows compare stage III (most severe) with stage I; stage II values are given in the statistic.
quote: the first stage – duration of the disease 1–2 days with an invasion intensity of 2–4%; the second stage – duration of 3–4 days with an invasion intensity of 5–8%; the third stage – duration of 5–6 days with an invasion intensity exceeding 9%.

severity_label: cerebral babesiosis vs all dogs with babesiosis
comparison_group: all dogs with babesiosis (n=136, includes the 11)
definition: Dogs with babesiosis (B. gibsoni, smear; PCR in the 11 neurological cases) showing neurological signs were classed as cerebral babesiosis; methods/abstract also cite Babesia in red cells of cerebrospinal fluid. The comparison group is all 136 babesiosis dogs, which includes the 11 cerebral cases.
quote: In this study, 11 of 136 positive Babesia individuals displayed neurological symptoms and were categorized as cerebral babesiosis.

complication: acute renal failure (fatal, proven at post mortem)
severity_label: acute renal failure proven on post mortem vs full recovery
definition: Among three dogs with the haemoconcentrating form of babesiosis seen during the study period, one had acute renal failure proven on post mortem examination and histopathology (died); two made a full recovery.
quote: The third dog had acute renal failure proven on post mortem examination and histopathology.

definition_source: as previously described (ref. 11, Keller et al. hypoglycaemia study)
definition: Admission plasma glucose <3.3 mmol/L (hypoglycaemic) vs 3.3-5.5 mmol/L (normoglycaemic); 12 dogs per group, recruited to fixed group sizes. Only dogs that survived to discharge were included; dogs with concurrent disease, E. canis or B. vogeli excluded.
quote: Three patient groups were recruited: hypoglycaemic dogs (glucose < 3.3 mmol/ , n = 12); normoglycaemic dogs (glucose 3.3–5.5 mmol/ , n = 12); hyperglycaemic dogs (glucose > 5.5 mmol/ , n = 12).

definition: Admission plasma glucose >5.5 mmol/L (hyperglycaemic) vs 3.3-5.5 mmol/L; 12 dogs per group; survivors only.
quote: Three patient groups were recruited: hypoglycaemic dogs (glucose < 3.3 mmol/ , n = 12); normoglycaemic dogs (glucose 3.3–5.5 mmol/ , n = 12); hyperglycaemic dogs (glucose > 5.5 mmol/ , n = 12).

definition: Dogs admitted to the OVAH ICU with PCR/RLB-confirmed B. rossi; outcome survived to discharge or died. Dogs euthanased for reasons other than poor prognosis were excluded, so euthanasia for poor prognosis is taken as counted with deaths.
quote: Outcome was recorded as the patient survived and was discharged or died.

severity_label: length of ICU stay (days hospitalised) in survivors
definition: Number of days of hospitalisation in the ICU among survivors (continuous).
quote: Among survivors, multiple regression analysis was used to examine the relationship between CRP concentration at admission and length of stay in ICU, adjusting for age and sex.

definition: Dogs that died despite imidocarb treatment (n = 2, both co-infected) or were euthanised at the owners' request (n = 2) versus dogs that clinically recovered after imidocarb (n = 41). Follow-up horizon not stated.
quote: Of the 45 dogs diagnosed with babesiosis, four (9%) died.

components: renal; hepatic or icterus; pulmonary; rhabdomyolysis
definition_source: Jacobson and Clark 1994 complications; bilirubin criterion from Weiser 1992 / Matijatko et al. 2009
definition: Complicated if one or more of: renal dysfunction (creatinine > 180 umol/l), hepatic dysfunction (ALT > 176 IU/l and AP > 360 IU/l, or bilirubin > 100 umol/l), respiratory dysfunction (radiographic pulmonary oedema or dyspnoea), muscular involvement (CPK > 600 IU/l). Complications seen: renal 5/7, hepatic 3/7, muscular 2/7, ARDS 1/7; 4 of 7 complicated dogs died.
quote: On the basis of clinical manifestations and laboratory data the affected dogs were divided into two groups: complicated (Group 1.1.) and uncomplicated (Group 1.2.) babesiosis (Jacobson and Clark, 1994).

severity_label: severe vs moderate vs mild anaemia (uncomplicated dogs only)
severe_group: moderate anaemia (n=9); severe n=1 not analysed
definition: Uncomplicated dogs graded by haematocrit: severe HCT < 16 (n=1), moderate 16 <= HCT < 35 (n=9), mild HCT >= 35 (n=18).
quote: Furthermore, depending on the severity of anaemia, dogs with uncomplicated babesiosis were classified as suffering from severe (haematocrit (HCT) < 16; Group 1.2.1.), moderate (16 ≤ HCT < 35; Group 1.2.2.), or mild disease (HCT ≥ 35; Group 1.2.3.) (Jacobson and Clark, 1994).

definition: Blood transfusion given at the attending clinician's discretion, as a general guideline when PCV <15 %, also guided by clinical status (e.g. collapse). The authors treat the transfused group as the more anaemic group.
quote: As a general guideline, dogs with PCV of <15 % were transfused, but in many cases the clinical status of the dog ( e.g. collapsed vs non-collapsed) played a role in decision-making.

definition: Infected dogs divided by serum urea and creatinine results into azotaemic and non-azotaemic groups; cut-offs not stated.
quote: The results allowed serum samples from group A to be divided into 2 groups: azotaemic (A1) and non-azotaemic (A2).

definition: Azotaemia = increased serum urea and creatinine concentrations above reference intervals; dogs with increased urea but normal creatinine were excluded.
quote: Azotaemia was detected in nine out of 23 dogs (39.13%; 95% CI - 17.55% to 60.71%, Group A).

definition: Serum creatinine as a continuous measure of renal dysfunction (azotaemia), correlated with thyroxin concentrations in all 23 dogs.
quote: Correlations between azotaemic parameters ( i.e. serum urea and creatinine) and TT4 and FT4 concentrations were calculated.

definition: Serum urea as a continuous measure of renal dysfunction (azotaemia), correlated with thyroxin concentrations in all 23 dogs.
quote: Correlations between azotaemic parameters ( i.e. serum urea and creatinine) and TT4 and FT4 concentrations were calculated.

definition: Dogs hospitalised (mean stay 1.74 days, up to 21 days) vs treated as outpatients. Criteria for hospitalisation not stated.
quote: Of the dogs diagnosed with Babesia, 41.9% (152/363) were hospitalised, whilst the rest were treated on an outpatient basis.

definition_source: modified Reyers et al. 1998 (cited by Jacobson) and Tvedten and Weiss
definition: PCV < 15% severe, 15-30% moderate, > 30-37% mild, > 37% non-anaemic (modified Reyers et al. 1998 / Jacobson and Tvedten and Weiss).
quote: Dogs with PCV less than 15% were considered as severely anaemic, and those with PCV 15–30 as moderately anaemic, those with PCV >30–37 as mildly anaemic, and those with PCV >37% as nonanaemic.

definition: PCV (and Hb) as a continuous measure of anaemia severity, compared between factor groups by ANOVA or correlated by Pearson's r.
quote: Overall mean PCV was 18.4% (±SD, range; ±9.2, 5.0–49.0) and overall mean Hb was 6.4 g/L (±SD, range; ±3.04, 1–14.1).
